item.title: Dortmund Beat Sabah 2-1, Guirassy Scores Twice
item.description: Borussia Dortmund beat Sabah Masazir 2-1 in Baku on Champions League matchday 3 on Tuesday (20/10/2026). Serhou Guirassy scored twice (10', 53') after Aden McCarthy had equalised in the 39th minute. Dortmund's first away UCL win in almost a year takes them to 6 points and ends a three-match winless run.
item.content:encoded:
Guirassy Puts Dortmund Ahead, McCarthy Equalises

Borussia Dortmund defeated Sabah Masazir 2-1 in UEFA Champions League 2026/2027 league-phase matchday 3 at Baku Olympic Stadium on Tuesday (20/10/2026). Serhou Guirassy's brace secured Die Borussen's first away win in the competition in almost a year.

Dortmund took the lead in the 10th minute. Felix Nmecha's fierce effort was parried by Sabah keeper Stas Pokatilov, and Guirassy was quickest to the rebound to make it 1-0.

The hosts, founded only in 2017, refused to fold. In the 39th minute, Aden McCarthy rose to head home Tymoteusz Puchacz's free-kick delivery. The 1-1 scoreline held until the break — and the Baku crowd dared to dream.

Guirassy's Second-Half Strike Proves Decisive

Dortmund came out stronger after the interval and retook the lead in the 53rd minute. Joey Veerman swung in a precise cross, and Guirassy met it with his left foot to make it 2-1.

Sabah pushed for an equaliser in the closing stages, but Niko Kovac's well-marshalled defence held firm until the final whistle. Dortmund took all three points back from Azerbaijan.

The stats reflected the visitors' dominance: 59 percent possession and 14 shots with six on target, against Sabah's seven shots (three on target).

Winless Run Ends, Dortmund Move to 6 Points

The victory ended Dortmund's three-match winless run in all competitions, which included the painful 0-1 defeat to Bodo/Glimt on matchday 2. It was also their first away Champions League win in almost a year — their last coming on 21 October 2025 in a 4-2 victory at FC Copenhagen.

With three more points, Dortmund now have six from three matches and are back on course in the race for the round of 16. Sabah remain on three points.

Guirassy was once again Dortmund's hero: the Guinea striker also scored twice in the 3-2 win over Villarreal on the opening matchday. His European form will be vital for Kovac's side in the big games ahead.

item.title: Fenerbahce Throw Away Win, Held 2-2 by Slavia Prague
item.description: Fenerbahce drew 2-2 with Slavia Prague in Istanbul on Champions League matchday 3 on Tuesday (20/10/2026). The hosts led through Oguz Aydin (4') and Mason Greenwood (11'), but Slavia replied via Lukas Provod (15') and Pavel Kacor's 90th-minute equaliser. Fenerbahce remain winless in three games.
item.content:encoded:
Fenerbahce Race Into 2-0 Lead Inside 11 Minutes

Fenerbahce were held to a 2-2 draw by Slavia Prague in UEFA Champions League 2026/2027 league-phase matchday 3 at Chobani Stadium, Istanbul, on Tuesday (20/10/2026). The hosts threw away a two-goal lead built inside the opening 11 minutes.

Only four minutes were on the clock when Oğuz Aydın fired Fenerbahce 1-0 up, finishing off Milan Skriniar's pass. Seven minutes later, Mason Greenwood doubled the advantage with a clinical finish after linking up with Nelson Semedo — 2-0 to the home side.

The perfect start had the Istanbul crowd roaring. Fenerbahce looked confident after last week's 6-0 humiliation at Aston Villa, and a first league-phase win seemed only a matter of time.

Provod Pulls One Back, Kacor Strikes Late

Slavia refused to lie down. In the 15th minute, Lukáš Provod halved the deficit to 2-1 after Mateo Guendouzi committed a horror error, losing the ball on the edge of his own box — a blunder the visitors ruthlessly punished.

The 2-1 scoreline held until half-time. Fenerbahce tried to control the game in the second half, but Slavia kept pressing for an equaliser.

The drama came at the death. In the 90th minute, Pavel Kacor struck the equaliser to silence Chobani Stadium. Slavia, 2-0 down early on, left with a precious point.

Fenerbahce Still Winless

The draw extends Fenerbahce's poor start in this season's Champions League. The Portuguese-coached side drew 1-1 with AS Roma on the opening matchday before being hammered 6-0 by Aston Villa — and now failed to win again despite leading by two goals.

Slavia Prague are also yet to taste victory: the Czech side lost 2-3 to Lens and 0-2 to Sabah in their first two games. But a point in Istanbul is valuable capital for climbing the league-phase table.

For a Fenerbahce side boasting big names like Ederson, N'Golo Kante and Romelu Lukaku, the pressure is mounting. Three games without a win leaves their round-of-16 hopes fading.

item.title: Papua's Raja Ampat: The World's Ultimate Underwater Paradise
item.description: Raja Ampat in Southwest Papua sits at the Coral Triangle's heart, hosting 1,300+ fish and 600 coral species. Here is your travel guide via Sorong.
item.content:encoded:
Raja Ampat, Heart of the Coral Triangle

Raja Ampat — meaning 'Four Kings' — is an archipelago of roughly 1,500 islands off the coast of Southwest Papua, Indonesia. Its name refers to four main islands: Waigeo, Misool, Salawati, and Batanta. The archipelago lies right in the heart of the Coral Triangle, an area recognized for possessing the highest marine biodiversity on the planet.

The waters of Raja Ampat are home to more than 1,300 fish species and around 600 coral species — equivalent to 75 percent of the world's known coral species. Scientists describe it as the richest coral reef ecosystem on Earth, and new species continue to be discovered to this day.

Encountering Mantas, Wobbegongs, and Pygmy Seahorses

For divers and snorkelers, every dive in Raja Ampat feels like an underwater safari. Giant manta rays frequently glide past cleaning stations, wobbegong sharks conceal themselves in reef crevices, while sea turtles and pygmy seahorses remain prime targets for macro photographers.

The wonder does not end beneath the surface. Clusters of karst islands rising above turquoise waters, dense rainforests, secluded lagoons, and red birds-of-paradise make Raja Ampat a complete destination for nature enthusiasts — even for non-divers.

Getting to Raja Ampat: Fly to Sorong, Ferry to Waisai

The primary gateway to Raja Ampat is the city of Sorong. Travelers fly into Domine Eduard Osok Airport from Jakarta, Makassar, Manado, or Bali, then continue their journey via public ferry or speedboat for approximately two hours to Waisai, the capital of Raja Ampat Regency on Waigeo Island.

Every foreign visitor entering Raja Ampat's waters — whether for diving or snorkeling — is required to purchase a marine park conservation permit valid for one year. Revenue generated from this permit directly funds local ranger patrols and conservation initiatives throughout the area.

Best Time to Visit: October to April

The optimal time to visit Raja Ampat is between October and April, when the seas are calmer, skies are clear, and underwater visibility reaches 15–30 meters with water temperatures between 27–29 degrees Celsius. The period from December to February marks the peak season, with manta ray activity at its height from December to March.

Do not miss the iconic panoramic vista from the summit of Piaynemo — a collection of verdant karst islands perched above turquoise seas — alongside Wayag in the north and Misool in the south. Given the journey's distance, allocate at least seven to ten days to thoroughly explore the archipelago.

item.title: Stuttgart Held to 1-1 Draw by Atlético Madrid
item.description: VfB Stuttgart drew 1-1 with Atlético Madrid in Champions League matchday 3 at the MHP Arena, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. Jamie Leweling put the hosts ahead in the 36th minute before Julián Álvarez levelled in the 47th — his first goal for Atlético since the summer transfer saga. The draw, featuring one red card, ended Stuttgart's perfect start.
item.content:encoded:
Leweling's Early Goal Puts Stuttgart Ahead

VfB Stuttgart had to settle for a 1-1 draw with Atlético Madrid in UEFA Champions League 2026/2027 league phase matchday 3 at the MHP Arena, Stuttgart, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. The dominant hosts failed to convert their superiority into victory.

Stuttgart took the lead in the 36th minute through Jamie Leweling. The German winger's strike rewarded the hosts' first-half dominance and sent the MHP Arena crowd wild. The 1-0 lead for Stuttgart held until half-time.

Throughout the first half, Stuttgart were the more aggressive side and controlled the match. Atlético Madrid, known for their disciplined defence, struggled to build attacks and spent much of the half pinned in their own territory.

Álvarez Levels After the Break

Atlético Madrid fought back early in the second half. Julián Álvarez scored the equalizer in the 47th minute, just two minutes after the second-half kickoff. The quick goal made it 1-1 and revived the visitors' hopes.

The goal was special for Álvarez as his first for Atlético Madrid since the summer transfer saga. The Argentina striker had pushed for a move to Barcelona but ultimately stayed — and he has now repaid the club's faith with an important Champions League goal.

The match grew feistier after the equalizer. The game also featured one red card, raising the temperature of the contest in the remaining minutes. But no further goals came before the final whistle.

Stuttgart Dominant but Wasteful

The match statistics showed clear home dominance. Stuttgart enjoyed 54 percent possession and fired 17 shots at the Atlético Madrid goal. But poor finishing was the hosts' main problem on the night.

The draw ended Stuttgart's bid for a perfect start to this season's Champions League. After winning their opening two matches, Die Schwaben failed to make it three in a row and had to settle for a point at home.

For Atlético Madrid, a point from the trip to Germany remains valuable. Álvarez's goal early in the second half showed the visitors' character and refusal to give up, even after being under pressure for much of the first half.

item.title: Napoli Edge Bodø/Glimt 4-3 in Seven-Goal Thriller
item.description: Napoli beat Bodø/Glimt 4-3 in Champions League matchday 3 in Naples, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. Matteo Politano's strike (2') and Scott McTominay's brace (41', 75') — his first goals since heart surgery — plus Odin Lurås Bjørtuft's own goal (88') sealed the Partenopei's first win of the season after defeats to Arsenal and Villarreal.
item.content:encoded:
Politano's Early Strike Cancelled by Hauge

Napoli edged a thrilling 4-3 duel against Bodø/Glimt in UEFA Champions League 2026/2027 league phase matchday 3 at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, Naples, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. Seven goals were scored in a dramatic encounter decided only in the closing minutes.

The hosts struck very early. Matteo Politano scored in the 2nd minute to send the Naples crowd wild. But the lead did not last: Jens Petter Hauge levelled at 1-1 in the 27th minute and silenced the stadium.

Napoli retook the lead just before half-time. Scott McTominay scored in the 41st minute to put the Partenopei 2-1 up at the break. The goal was special as the midfielder's first since undergoing heart surgery.

Second-Half Drama Until the Own Goal

Bodø/Glimt refused to surrender in the second half. Andreas Helmersen levelled at 2-2 in the 63rd minute and threw the match wide open again. The Norwegian visitors showed remarkable mentality despite playing at the home of one of Italy's giants.

Scott McTominay was Napoli's hero once more. The Scotland midfielder scored his second in the 75th minute to put the hosts 3-2 up. The brace completed a special night for the player in his comeback match at Europe's highest level.

Napoli's victory was finally sealed in dramatic fashion in the 88th minute. Odin Lurås Bjørtuft scored an own goal that made it 4-2 and practically locked up the three points for the hosts. Sondre Fet added a late consolation in the 90th minute plus four, but it was too late for the visitors.

First Win and McTominay's Night

The 4-3 victory was Napoli's first in the Champions League this season. The Partenopei had previously lost to Arsenal and Villarreal, making the three points against Bodø/Glimt vital to keep their hopes of progressing from the league phase alive.

The night also belonged to Scott McTominay. His two goals — his first since heart surgery — proved the midfielder's resurgence and dedication to returning to his best. The Naples crowd gave him a warm reception for his fight.

For Bodø/Glimt, the defeat was painful after twice fighting back to level. But the late own goal proved the difference, and the Norwegian side returned home pointless from their trip to Italy.

item.title: Liverpool Fight Back from 0-2 to Beat Villarreal 4-3
item.description: Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 in Champions League matchday 3 at Anfield, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB, after coming from 2-0 down. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice (36', 65'), Ronald Araújo (45+1') and Florian Wirtz (68') added to the tally, while 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha provided two assists. A third straight win keeps the Reds' perfect European record intact.
item.content:encoded:
2-0 Down, Liverpool Fight Back Before the Break

Liverpool won a dramatic 4-3 duel against Villarreal in UEFA Champions League 2026/2027 league phase matchday 3 at Anfield, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. The hosts fell two goals behind before fighting back to seal victory in a seven-goal thriller.

Villarreal stunned the hosts with two early goals. Georges Mikautadze put the visitors ahead in the 4th minute, before Sergi Cardona doubled the lead to 2-0 in the 29th minute. Anfield fell silent watching their team trail by two at home.

Liverpool responded swiftly. Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back in the 36th minute, and Ronald Araújo levelled at 2-2 in the 45th minute plus one at the end of the first half. Two goals in the final ten minutes of the half turned the match around and restored the hosts' belief.

Mac Allister and Wirtz Turn It Around

Liverpool were far more aggressive after the restart and finally took the lead. Alexis Mac Allister scored his second in the 65th minute to put the Reds 3-2 ahead — a goal that sent Anfield into delirium.

Three minutes later, Florian Wirtz extended the lead to 4-2 in the 68th minute. The goal felt special for the German midfielder as his first since April, ending a long drought that had weighed on him.

Villarreal refused to give up and pulled one back through Tani Oluwaseyi in the 87th minute. But there was not enough time left for the visitors to level, and Liverpool closed out a dramatic 4-3 victory.

Teenage Star Ngumoha and a Perfect Record

The real star of the night was Rio Ngumoha. The 18-year-old dazzled with two assists that proved key to Liverpool's comeback. His maturity at such a young age left the Anfield crowd in awe.

The victory also preserved Liverpool's perfect Champions League record this season: three wins from three matches. The Reds showed championship character in coming from two goals down — a win their supporters will remember for a long time.

For the visitors, coach Andoni Iraola had done his utmost with six substitutions throughout the match. But the changes were not enough to stem Liverpool's second-half wave, and Villarreal went home empty-handed.

item.title: PSG Thrash Barcelona 4-2 as Dembélé Suffers Injury
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 in Champions League matchday 3 at the Parc des Princes, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. Goals from Désiré Doué (38'), Lucas Hernández (72'), Vitinha (81') and Fabián Ruiz (86') secured the win despite Barcelona twice levelling through Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal. The victory came at a cost with Ousmane Dembélé injured in the 20th minute.
item.content:encoded:
Twice Pegged Back, PSG Still Win 4-2

Paris Saint-Germain defeated Barcelona 4-2 in UEFA Champions League 2026/2027 league phase matchday 3 at the Parc des Princes, Paris, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. Six goals were scored in a dramatic encounter that twice saw Barcelona fight back to level before finally succumbing late on.

The hosts took the lead in the 38th minute through Désiré Doué. The young Frenchman's strike put PSG 1-0 up, a lead they held until half-time. Barcelona, despite enjoying more possession, struggled to break down the hosts' compact defence in the first half.

Barcelona finally levelled ten minutes after the restart. Xavi Espart scored in the 55th minute to make it 1-1 and revive the visitors' hopes. But PSG retook the lead through Lucas Hernández's header in the 72nd minute, sending the Parc des Princes crowd into raptures.

The drama was not over. Lamine Yamal levelled again at 2-2 in the 79th minute, and the match looked destined for a draw. Yet PSG showed championship mentality in the final five minutes: Vitinha scored in the 81st minute to make it 3-2, before Fabián Ruiz sealed the 4-2 win in the 86th minute from Achraf Hakimi's assist.

Dembélé Injured, Two More Stars Withdrawn

PSG's convincing win came at a heavy price. Ousmane Dembélé, the Ballon d'Or winner, was forced off in the 20th minute with a hamstring injury and replaced by Ferran Torres. The injury is bad news for PSG, who rely heavily on the winger's pace in attack.

PSG's problems did not stop there. Two more stars, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos, were also withdrawn in the second half. Losing three key players in one match made the 4-2 victory over Barcelona feel bittersweet for the hosts, with a congested schedule still ahead domestically and in Europe.

Dembélé's condition is now the main concern. The forward is expected to undergo further examination to determine the severity of the hamstring injury and how long he will be sidelined.

PSG More Clinical Despite Less Possession

The match statistics reflected the hosts' aggression. PSG fired 22 shots with 15 on target, compared to 18 shots with only five on target for Barcelona. Clinical finishing proved the decisive difference between the two sides.

Interestingly, Barcelona dominated possession with 53 percent. But the Blaugrana's dominance produced few dangerous chances, while every PSG attack looked threatening.

Two goals in the final five minutes underlined the sharpness of PSG's attack. Despite losing Dembélé as early as the 20th minute, Les Parisiens still scored four goals against one of Europe's strongest teams — a firm statement of their Champions League ambitions this season.

item.title: Foden Hat-trick Fires Man City to 5-1 Win Over AEK
item.description: Manchester City beat AEK Athens 5-1 in Champions League matchday 3 at the Etihad, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. Phil Foden scored a hat-trick (34', 66', 76') — the fourth of his City career — alongside goals from Elliot Anderson (12') and Rayan Cherki (57'). The win was a response to last week's PSG defeat, achieved without Erling Haaland as 17-year-old Floyd Samba started.
item.content:encoded:
Anderson and Foden Put City Two Up

Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1 in UEFA Champions League 2026/2027 league phase matchday 3 at the Etihad Stadium, early Wednesday (21/10/2026) WIB. Phil Foden was the star of the show with a hat-trick that powered his side to a convincing victory.

City took the lead in the 12th minute through Elliot Anderson. The early goal gave the hosts confidence as they kept pressing the AEK Athens defence. Phil Foden doubled the lead to 2-0 in the 34th minute, a scoreline that held until half-time.

AEK Athens briefly threatened early in the second half. Stavros Pilios pulled one back to make it 2-1 in the 52nd minute and briefly worried the Etihad crowd. But City's response was swift and ruthless.

Cherki and Two More for Foden

Rayan Cherki restored City's two-goal cushion in the 57th minute. The Frenchman's strike broke the visitors' momentum and opened the floodgates for the hosts in the remainder of the match.

Phil Foden then added two more goals in the 66th and 76th minutes to complete his hat-trick and make it 5-1. Each strike was greeted with roars from the supporters packing the Etihad Stadium.

The hat-trick against AEK Athens was recorded as the fourth of Phil Foden's Manchester City career. The England midfielder's brilliant display proved once again that he remains one of the most decisive players in Enzo Maresca's squad.

The Perfect Response After the PSG Defeat

The emphatic victory was the perfect response from Manchester City after their defeat to PSG last week. Three points against AEK Athens also marked City's second Champions League win this season and kept their league-phase hopes alive.

Notably, City achieved this big win without Erling Haaland, who was not involved. In his place, 17-year-old striker Floyd Samba was trusted to start — a bold decision that underlined the depth of City's squad.

With this 5-1 victory, Manchester City sent a firm message to their European rivals. Their attack remains razor-sharp even without their main goal machine, and Phil Foden once again proved himself the difference-maker on the big stage.

item.title: 152 Hikers Evacuated as Forest Fire Hits Mount Sumbing in Wonosobo
item.description: A forest fire swept through the Mount Sumbing area in Wonosobo Regency, Central Java, on Monday afternoon (10/19/2026). A total of 152 registered hikers from Garung and Gajahmungkur basecamps were evacuated by basecamp teams together with a joint team. All hikers were reported safe.
item.content:encoded:
Fire Detected Monday Afternoon

Wonosobo — A forest fire broke out in the Mount Sumbing area of Wonosobo Regency, Central Java, on Monday (10/19/2026) at around 3:00 PM local time. The fire was first reported by climbing porters on the Gajahmungkur route in Kalikajar District.

Flames were spotted at Plot 29 of RPH Kleseman, BKPH Wonosobo, KPH Kedu Utara, at an altitude of 2,500 to 2,709 meters above sea level. Strong winds and dry vegetation made the fire difficult to contain.

152 Hikers Evacuated, All Safe

Sumekto Hendro, head of the Wonosobo Disaster Mitigation Agency (BPBD), said 152 registered hikers were evacuated from two climbing routes: Garung Basecamp and Gajahmungkur Basecamp. "The basecamp teams together with the joint team have evacuated 152 hikers according to registration," Sumekto said.

All hikers were reported safe and were descending. Sabarno, coordinator of the BPBD Wonosobo Rapid Response Team, had earlier cited 71 hikers based on information from a basecamp chief — also safe. As of Monday night there were no reports of injuries or fatalities.

Firefighting Resumes Tuesday Morning

Manual firefighting efforts by the joint team from several basecamps on Monday night failed to put out the flames due to strong winds and very dry vegetation above. Nighttime operations were not possible.

A full-scale firefighting operation resumed on Tuesday morning (10/20/2026). The cause of the fire and the size of the affected area are still being assessed.

item.title: 53 Soldiers Killed in Houthi Missile Strike on Yemen's Shabwa Military Camp
item.description: Three Houthi ballistic missiles struck the Al-Alam military training camp in Jardan, Shabwa, southern Yemen, on Monday (19/10/2026). At least 53 personnel were killed and around 200 injured — one of the deadliest attacks since Yemen's civil war reignited. The Houthis acknowledged the strike; Yemen's government pledged a firm response.
item.content:encoded:
Three Ballistic Missiles Hit Training Camp

Shabwa — At least 53 military personnel were killed and around 200 injured after three Houthi-launched ballistic missiles struck the Al-Alam military training camp in Jardan district, Shabwa province, southern Yemen, on Monday (19/10/2026).

According to the Shabwa provincial government, the missiles hit as new recruits of the internal security forces — the Rapid Intervention unit — were lining up for a training session. The casualties were evacuated to hospitals in Ataq, the provincial capital, which were reported overwhelmed by the wounded. The toll is described as preliminary and may rise.

Houthis Claim Attack, Government Vows Firm Response

The Houthis acknowledged the strike. Their military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, claimed the target was a "Saudi enemy gathering" and alleged Saudi personnel were among the casualties — claims offered without evidence and not yet addressed by Saudi authorities.

Rashad Al-Alimi, chairman of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, strongly condemned the attack and pledged a "firm response". The Shabwa provincial government urged the central government and the coalition to urgently provide air defence and early warning systems to strengthen the province's defences.

Worst Escalation Since War Reignited

The strike is described as one of the deadliest single attacks since Yemen's civil war reignited in September, after the 2022 ceasefire deal collapsed. Government forces this month launched a campaign to recapture Houthi-held areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea.

The Yemen conflict has become one front in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran, with the Houthis in recent weeks repeatedly striking Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh's international airport and Saudi Aramco oil facilities.

item.title: Kenya Cult Leader Convicted of 191 Murders
item.description: Kenya's Mombasa High Court convicted cult leader Paul Mackenzie of 191 murders—190 children—in the Shakahola starvation tragedy. Sentencing is Nov. 6, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Historic Verdict in Mombasa

Mombasa — The Mombasa High Court in Kenya on Monday (10/19/2026) found cult leader Paul Mackenzie guilty of 191 counts of murder—190 of whom were children. Alongside approximately 30 co-defendants, Mackenzie was tried over the mass forced-fasting tragedy in Shakahola Forest, Kilifi County, one of the most shocking criminal cases in modern Kenyan history.

The delivery of the verdict by Judge Lady Justice Diana Kavedza lasted more than eight hours. The court concluded that the victims' deaths were the result of an 'organized system' that coerced followers into fasting to death. Prosecutors called the trial one of the most historic criminal cases Kenya has ever handled.

An Organized Forced-Fasting System

The Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions of Kenya stated that the court found religious teachings and the cult's hierarchy were utilized to 'direct and enforce a lethal fast' upon Mackenzie's followers. 'The fasting was carried out sequentially, starting with the children, while guards controlled movements and prevented followers from escaping,' the office stated in an official release.

Evidence presented included WhatsApp messages from Mackenzie's phone showing communication with followers before their move to Shakahola, as well as testimony that children were detained, denied food, and punished if they attempted to eat or flee.

Mackenzie, who ran Good News International Church, allegedly ordered his followers to fast to death to 'meet Jesus' before the apocalypse. The court also heard that Mackenzie forbade modern medicine and formal education for his followers.

Chilling facts emerged from autopsy findings: several victims did not die solely of starvation, but rather from asphyxiation, strangulation, or head trauma.

429 Bodies Since 2023, Sentencing on November 6

The Shakahola tragedy unfolded in April 2023 when police began exhuming shallow graves across the forest. To date, 429 bodies have been recovered from an area spanning 325 hectares. Murder charges against Mackenzie and his co-defendants were filed in 2024.

Mackenzie's defense announced plans to appeal. Defense attorney Lawrence Obonyo stated that his client maintains he never forced anyone to fast and described the victims' actions as a voluntary choice—an argument flatly rejected by the court.

Sentencing for Mackenzie and his co-defendants will be handed down on November 6, 2026. Prosecutors noted that additional charges could follow as investigations continue into hundreds of other bodies that remain unidentified.

item.title: Students Rally on Two Years of Prabowo-Gibran, Bring 5 Demands
item.description: The Komite Sadar student alliance rallies in Jakarta marking two years of Prabowo-Gibran with five demands. Labor groups skip as police prepare traffic plans.
item.content:encoded:
Five Demands of Komite Sadar

A student alliance organized under Komite Sadar (Save People's Sovereignty) is scheduled to hold a demonstration in Jakarta on Tuesday (10/20/2026), marking exactly two years of President Prabowo Subianto and Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's administration. According to organizers cited by AFU.id, the itinerary begins with a symbolic demonstration around the Tugu Proklamasi area in the morning, followed by a mass rally at the Tugu Tani area from afternoon to evening.

During the demonstration, Komite Sadar is bringing five primary demands. First, urging the government to declare forest and land fires (karhutla) and flooding as national disasters, rehabilitate the health of affected citizens, prosecute corporations deemed responsible for the crises, and revoke their permits. Second, reforming economic policy governance and restoring market confidence. Third, ending restrictions on freedom of speech. Fourth, eradicating corruption, collusion, and nepotism (KKN). Fifth, lowering the cost of education, healthcare, and public services while ensuring more equitable access for the public.

Ahead of the rally, Komite Sadar also released survey results reportedly involving 560 respondents spanning Sumatra to Papua. According to the survey, 78.8 percent of respondents reportedly assessed the Prabowo-Gibran administration and its cabinet as failing to resolve key public issues. AFU.id noted that these figures have not yet been accompanied by an open publication of the methodology. The same survey indicated that environmental issues were the biggest concern among respondents—with 83.5 percent highlighting deforestation and forest fires, 71.1 percent pointing to high prices of basic necessities, and 70.6 percent citing corruption and abuse of power.

Who Joins, Who Skips

Komite Sadar consists of students from several higher education institutions, including Universitas Indonesia (UI), Bandung Institute of Technology (ITB), Padjadjaran University, Diponegoro University, Semarang State University, Gadjah Mada University (UGM), UPN Veteran Yogyakarta, Airlangga University, and Brawijaya University. Several campuses plan to stage rallies in their respective regions, while the Jakarta action will be centered at the two designated locations.

On the other hand, labor groups have taken a different stance. Andi Gani Nena Wea, President of the Confederation of All Indonesian Workers' Unions (KSPSI), stated that the Indonesian Labor Struggle Coalition (KBPBI) would not hold demonstrations on October 20. As reported by Kebaruan.com, Andi Gani, speaking in Nganjuk on Saturday (10/17/2026), considered the date too volatile, prompting his coalition to observe the day with community service instead. He also clarified the intent of earlier labor protests on September 25 and October 6, stating they were meant to voice aspirations rather than mount opposition against the President.

Authorities and educational institutions have also taken precautions. The West Java Education Agency issued a circular dated October 16, 2026, requesting students of senior high schools (SMA), vocational high schools (SMK), and special education schools (SLB)—both public and private—to steer clear of demonstrations, while the Chief of Banten Regional Police (Polda Banten) visited several schools to urge students not to take to the streets.

Assembly Points and Traffic Advisories

In Jakarta, crowds are expected to gather at two assembly points in Central Jakarta: the Tugu Tani area on Jalan Raya Kebon Sirih and Tugu Proklamasi in Menteng. The Traffic Directorate of the Jakarta Metro Regional Police (Ditlantas Polda Metro Jaya) has prepared traffic diversion plans to anticipate the impact of the events.

According to KabarKampus.com, thoroughfares potentially impacted by congestion include areas surrounding the State Palace, the National Monument (Monas), Jalan Sudirman-Thamrin, and the House of Representatives/People's Consultative Assembly (DPR/MPR RI) building. Traffic Director of Polda Metro Jaya Senior Commissioner (Kombes Pol) Firman Darmansyah urged the public to anticipate travel times and choose alternative routes if they have no urgent business around the demonstration sites. Traffic management measures will be implemented situationally based on field conditions, and residents are advised to follow officers' instructions.

item.title: 2 Years of Prabowo: Gerindra's Stability Claims vs Economic Data
item.description: Two years of Prabowo-Gibran: Gerindra claims self-reliance and stable welfare; BPS logs 5.45% H1 2026 growth and 8.07% poverty, but SMRC sees approval at 51.1%.
item.content:encoded:
Gerindra’s Claim: Self-Reliance and Stable Welfare

The Gerindra Party (Great Indonesia Movement Party) assessed that two years of the Prabowo-Gibran administration—marking exactly two years on Tuesday, October 20, 2026—demonstrated progress in strengthening national self-reliance and public welfare. The assessment was conveyed by party spokesperson Sugiat Santoso in a statement on Monday (10/19/2026).

“Two years of the Prabowo-Gibran administration show progress in strengthening national self-reliance and public welfare. This is evident from economic fundamentals that remain stable amid global volatility, strengthening food production, expanding access to education and healthcare, and accelerating downstreaming,” Sugiat said.

A similar sentiment was expressed by Menko Perekonomian (Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs) Airlangga Hartarto at the Presidential Palace on the same day: “Alhamdulillah, the situation is relatively stable, politically, economically, and socially.” The next target, he said, is higher growth and more equitable welfare.

BPS Data: 5.45 Percent Growth, Poverty Decreases

Data from BPS (Statistics Indonesia) summarized in an analysis by Kompas.com (10/15/2026) showed the economy grew by 5.45 percent in the first semester of 2026, up from 4.99 percent in the same period of 2025. The second quarter of 2026 grew by 5.29 percent year-on-year.

The poverty rate dropped from 9.03 percent or 25.22 million people (March 2024) to 8.07 percent or 22.93 million people (March 2026)—a reduction of about 2.29 million people in two years. Open unemployment edged down from 4.82 to 4.68 percent, workers' wages rose from Rp 3.04 million to Rp 3.29 million, and the Gini ratio improved from 0.375 to 0.368.

BPS recorded annual inflation in September 2026 at 3.28 percent with an IHK (Consumer Price Index) of 112.31—still within the national target range of 2.5±1 percent. Monthly inflation was recorded at 0.30 percent and core inflation at 2.84 percent.

Flagship Programs: MBG, CKG, and Food Self-Sufficiency

The CKG (Free Health Checkup) program was reported to reach 99.1 million people; MBG (Free Nutritious Meals) reached around 57 million beneficiaries as of August 2026; and Sekolah Rakyat (People's Schools) operated in 182 locations with 44,000 students.

The government claims self-sufficiency in eight commodities: rice, corn, large chili, bird's eye chili, consumption sugar, chicken meat, chicken eggs, and shallots. A total of 145 fertilizer distribution regulations were simplified and the HET (Highest Retail Price) for subsidized fertilizer dropped 20 percent since October 2025. September 2026 NTP (Farmer Terms of Trade) was recorded at 131.11—up 1.49 percent monthly.

Danantara recorded 26 strategic projects valued at Rp 225 trillion with a projection of 37,833 workers. Satgas PKH (Forestry Area Governance Task Force) regained control of 6.22 million hectares of forest areas up to October 6, 2026.

Critical Notes: Public Surveys and Fiscal Pressures

CELIOS (Center of Economic and Law Studies) alongside the Shadow Cabinet (released 10/11/2026): 75 percent of 1,122 respondents admitted to feeling stressed over government policies—the main complaints being rising staple food prices, lack of jobs, and law enforcement. Gerindra rejected the report, calling it unobjective.

Esa Unggul University observer Jamiluddin Ritonga (10/19/2026) assessed that there is a gap between government claims and public perception. The SMRC (Saiful Mujani Research and Consulting) survey from October 1–10, 2026 showed: public satisfaction dropped from 81.2 percent (November 2025) to 51.1 percent (July 2026); Prabowo's electability stood at 9.8 percent—below Dedi Mulyadi (35.5 percent) and Anies Baswedan (10.3 percent).

On the budget side, the Kompas analysis noted that Regional Transfers fell from Rp 857.6 trillion (25.8 percent of spending, 2024 APBN (State Revenue and Expenditure Budget)) to Rp 693 trillion (around 18 percent, 2026 APBN). The analysis cautioned: differences in baseline conditions and geopolitics across eras limit conclusions that all achievements were solely driven by the incumbent president.

item.title: Guterres Urges UN Council Reform, Indonesia Eyes 2029–2030 Seat
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged reform of the UN Security Council at a forum in Jakarta on Monday (19/10/2026), judging that the composition of its five permanent members is no longer relevant and that some of its members are instead triggering wars. Amid growing proposals for a permanent African seat and restrictions on the veto, Indonesia reaffirmed its support for reform while also putting itself forward as a candidate for a non-permanent Security Council seat for the 2029–2030 term.
item.content:encoded:
Guterres: UN Security Council Composition No Longer Reflects the World

UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for an overhaul of the UN Security Council (UNSC) structure because the composition of its permanent members is considered to no longer reflect current world conditions. The statement was made by Guterres at the Foreign Policy Circle Talks forum titled 'Eight Decades of the United Nations: What's Next?' at the Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Central Jakarta, Monday (19/10/2026), attended by Indonesian Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir.

"We must also reform the Security Council. The permanent members of the Security Council currently consist of three European countries, one North American country, and one Asian country. Is this composition relevant to today's world? Does this body reflect the realities of today's world? Clearly not," said Guterres.

Guterres also highlighted the bitter irony that several permanent members are themselves involved in triggering armed conflict. "Unfortunately, today we are seeing permanent members of the Security Council sometimes starting wars while disregarding international law, which ultimately severely limits the UN's ability to advance world peace and security," he said. The statement was made at the close of his official visit to Indonesia, October 17–19, 2026, which included a meeting with President Prabowo Subianto and a review of the Indonesian National Armed Forces (TNI) Peacekeeping Mission Center (PMPP) in Bogor.

Proposals on the Table: African Seats to Veto Limits

The UN Security Council currently has 15 members: five permanent members — the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Russia and China — each holding veto power, plus ten non-permanent members elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms. This composition has barely changed since the UN was founded in 1945.

A number of concrete proposals have emerged. The African Union's Ezulwini Consensus demands at least two permanent seats for Africa with the same rights and privileges as current permanent members, including veto power. Guterres has repeatedly supported it — at the 81st UN General Assembly in September 2026 he asserted that a 21st-century Security Council without a permanent African seat is unjust and indefensible. Spain went further by proposing the abolition of veto power altogether, while the French-Mexican initiative pushes for restricting the use of the veto in cases of mass atrocities.

Its biggest challenge is structural: amending the UN Charter requires the support of two-thirds of the General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of member states, including all five veto holders — meaning any veto holder can block reforms that curtail its own power.

Indonesia's Position: Non-Permanent Member Candidate 2029–2030

Indonesia is taking an active role in this reform discourse. In a bilateral meeting with Guterres, Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir conveyed three strategic messages: commitment to UNSC reform along with Indonesia's candidacy as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for the 2029–2030 period, strengthening multilateralism, and support for Palestine.

The candidacy was announced by Foreign Minister Sugiono at the 81st UN General Assembly in New York, 26 September 2026, with the campaign theme 'Fostering Unity, Advancing Peace'. Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir emphasized that, if elected, Indonesia would push for a more effective, representative, transparent, and democratic Security Council. "The Security Council must be a space for creating solutions, not a space where vetoes occur," he stressed.

Indonesia is no newcomer to the UNSC: it has held a non-permanent seat four times, in 1973–1974, 1995–1996, 2007–2008, and 2019–2020, and held the UNSC presidency in August 2020. Indonesia is also among the largest contributors of UN peacekeeping troops since 1957, including a long-term assignment in Lebanon through UNIFIL.

item.title: Wildfire Protest in C. Kalimantan: Governor's Office Sealed Off
item.description: Hundreds sealed the Central Kalimantan governor's office on Monday (19/10/2026) after Governor Agustiar Sabran failed to return, issuing a 72-hour ultimatum.
item.content:encoded:
Governor Leaves and Fails to Return

Hundreds of residents joined under the Central Kalimantan People Against Alliance held a Chapter III protest in front of the Central Kalimantan Governor's Office in Palangka Raya on Monday (19/10/2026). The rally, titled 'Emergency Warning for Forest and Land Fires and Smog', grew heated after Central Kalimantan Governor Agustiar Sabran, who had briefly met the crowd, left the premises and did not return as promised.

Residents' frustration peaked as the crowd broke through perimeter barriers into the front yard of the governor's office. In front of the main entrance to Jayang Tingang Hall, they unfurled a banner reading 'OFFICE SEALED BY THE PEOPLE' as a symbolic protest against what they deemed sluggish handling of karhutla (kebakaran hutan dan lahan - forest and land fires).

Sealing Banner and Nine Wildfire Demands

Protest field coordinator Sugianto stated that the crowd had been waiting since midday, but the governor never returned. According to him, Agustiar instead left to meet other officials out of town—a move that deeply disappointed the demonstrators. Sugianto added that the public has run out of patience waiting for serious action on the wildfires that have suffocated Central Kalimantan residents for months.

During the demonstration, the crowd submitted nine demands. These included declaring a state of disaster emergency for forest and land fires and smog across all of Central Kalimantan, conducting a comprehensive environmental audit of plantation and mining permits, imposing a moratorium on issuing new permits on peatlands, enforcing the law against land-burning corporations, and ensuring transparency in disaster management funds.

72-Hour Ultimatum

The demonstrators also issued a firm ultimatum to the Central Kalimantan Provincial Government. 'If within three times 24 hours there is no serious response from the Central Kalimantan Provincial Government, we will return with a larger crowd,' Sugianto said. The primary demand urged by the crowd was declaring the wildfires a national disaster—a call also echoed by BEM UI (Badan Eksekutif Mahasiswa Universitas Indonesia - Student Executive Board of Universitas Indonesia), which joined the Chapter III action with a 48-hour deadline.

As of 21:00 WIB (Waktu Indonesia Barat - Western Indonesia Time), neither Governor Agustiar Sabran nor the Central Kalimantan Provincial Government had issued an official written statement specifically addressing the nine demands.

Authorities: Peaceful Protest, No Arrests

Chief of Palangka Raya City Police AKBP (Ajun Komisaris Besar Polisi - Police Grand Commissioner Attendant) Yudha Satria stated that authorities respect citizens peacefully voicing their aspirations. He noted that brief tension arose when protesters pushed the perimeter fence, but the situation was brought under control and concluded peacefully.

Yudha emphasized that there were no arrests and no significant damage to buildings. He urged all parties to remain orderly and express their aspirations through lawful channels without violating regulations.

item.title: Bogor Busker Arrested After Forcing Angkot Passengers for Cash
item.description: Busker AL (25) was arrested by Bogor City Police after a viral video showed him coercing passengers on public minibus route 03 on Sunday (10/18/2026).
item.content:encoded:
Viral on Bogor's Angkot 03

A street busker identified by the initials AL (25) was taken into custody by the Satreskrim (Criminal Investigation Unit) of Polresta Bogor Kota (Bogor City Police Department) after a video showing him forcefully asking for money from passengers on an angkot (public minivan) went viral on social media. The incident occurred on angkot route 03 serving the BTM (Bogor Trade Mall) to Bogor Station route on Sunday afternoon (10/18/2026).

In the circulating video, AL distributed six envelopes to six passengers after finishing his singing. He then asked for the envelopes back with money inside while staring intensely at the passengers—behavior suspected to be a form of intimidation. The busker was also seen objecting to being recorded and reprimanded the person filming, Zahra (22).

Arrested Later That Night

Bogor City Police's Head of Public Relations Section, Second Police Inspector (Ipda) Imam, confirmed that AL was apprehended on Sunday night (10/18/2026) around the Town Square on Jalan Kapten Muslihat, Bogor City, shortly after the video spread widely. 'The perpetrator has been secured by the Sat Reskrim of Bogor Police,' he stated when confirmed by journalists on Monday (10/19/2026).

According to Imam, demanding back envelopes filled with money caused discomfort and fear among passengers. AL was reportedly cooperative during his arrest and admitted to carrying out the act to buy food.

The short video rapidly spread across various social media platforms and sparked outrage among netizens. Many felt that demanding money forcefully in confined public spaces like an angkot falls into the category of extortion rather than mere busking. Others highlighted the courage of Zahra in recording the event as evidence for reporting to the police.

Rehabilitated by Social Services and Satpol PP

Police stated they will coordinate with Dinsos (Social Services Agency) and Satpol PP (Civil Service Police Unit) to provide rehabilitation and guidance for AL. This case once again highlights the phenomenon of buskers in angkots who often cause public unrest—on one hand serving as a livelihood, but on the other potentially compromising safety and comfort in public transportation.

Bogor City Police urged the public to continue actively reporting any occurrences that could potentially disrupt security and public order so they can be followed up immediately.

The phenomenon of buskers coercing passengers is not new in Bogor City. The Department of Transportation alongside the police had repeatedly conducted enforcement operations, yet similar practices often resurface. Police hope this firm action will have a deterrent effect while opening pathways for rehabilitation so that the perpetrator can transition to more decent employment.

item.title: Fake WhatsApp on Play Store Surpasses 500,000 Downloads
item.description: A counterfeit WhatsApp app on Google Play reached over 500k downloads before disappearing on Monday, exploiting Early Access and mimicking the real app.
item.content:encoded:
500,000 Downloads of the Fake App

A counterfeit WhatsApp application circulating on the Google Play Store was downloaded more than 500,000 times before finally disappearing from the app store on Monday (19/10/2026). The finding was first revealed by Reddit user 2ne1cheese and reported by tech outlet Android Authority.

The fake application was published by a developer named 'Agment Assets sallu'—an account that had no other apps on the Play Store. Its store listing was crafted to look convincing: the icon, screenshots, and description text mirrored the official WhatsApp identically. The fraudulent listing even appeared as a sponsored search result, placed directly above the legitimate WhatsApp app.

Play Store Early Access Loophole

The counterfeit app's modus operandi exploited a loophole in Google Play's Early Access feature. Applications enrolled in the program do not show public reviews, making it difficult for users to distinguish authentic apps from fakes. This loophole contributed to deceiving 500,000 users.

By comparison, the official WhatsApp has surpassed 10 billion downloads on the Play Store, holding an Editors' Choice badge alongside hundreds of millions of reviews. As of Monday morning, the fake listing was no longer found, though Google has not issued an official confirmation regarding its removal.

This incident is not unprecedented. Previously, a fraudulent Google Chrome app also slipped through and garnered more than 100,000 downloads before being taken down. The same pattern recurred: cloning the name and icon of a popular app, then promoting it via sponsored search slots to appear legitimate to everyday users.

How to Identify the Authentic App

WhatsApp (Meta) emphasized that it does not support unauthorized applications. 'We do not support these third-party apps because we can't validate their security practices,' the company stated on its support page. While there is currently no verified evidence of data theft by the application, cybersecurity experts warn that such clones pose serious risks of stealing personal data or injecting malware.

Users are urged to always verify the developer's name prior to downloading—official WhatsApp is published by Meta—as well as look for the Editors' Choice badge and total download count. Do not rely solely on top-ranking search results, including those labeled as sponsored ads.

To verify whether the app installed on your phone is authentic, visit the official WhatsApp page on Google Play Store and check whether it shows as already installed. If the official page does not recognize the installation on your device, uninstall the application immediately and reinstall it from the official page.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Postpones FII Investment Forum Amid Houthi Attacks
item.description: Saudi Arabia has delayed its flagship Future Investment Initiative (FII) in Riyadh to 2027 following deadly Houthi missile and drone strikes on King Khalid Airport.
item.content:encoded:
Postponement officially announced

Saudi Arabia has officially postponed its flagship international investment forum, the Future Investment Initiative (FII), dubbed 'Davos in the Desert', to 2027. The 10th edition, themed 'The Power of Legacy', was originally scheduled to take place from October 26 to 29, 2026, in Riyadh.

The announcement was delivered by the FII Institute via an official email to several media outlets, including CNN and The National. In the statement, organizers noted that the decision was taken 'to ensure this historic tenth edition delivers the full scale, quality, and impact expected by partners, members, speakers, and delegates.' New dates in 2027 will be announced shortly, and all existing registrations and partnerships remain valid.

This marks only the second time FII has been canceled or postponed in its history—the first occurring in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. While the official FII statement did not explicitly cite the Houthi attacks, the timing of the announcement made the connection difficult to dispute.

Houthi airport attack serves as catalyst

The postponement follows a wave of missile and drone strikes launched by the Iran-backed Houthi movement into Saudi territory. The deadliest attack occurred on October 10, when a Houthi missile struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh—killing 13 people and injuring more than 300.

Saudi forces and the Houthis are now trading missile, drone, and airstrikes on a near-daily basis, with the conflict escalating sharply in recent weeks. Saudi authorities also reported that another projectile hit the southern city of Najran over the weekend, injuring six people.

Several nations have issued travel advisories, including the US State Department (Department of State), which urged American citizens in the Middle East to exercise heightened vigilance.

Wall Street chiefs pull back

This year's FII speaker lineup featured some of the biggest names in global finance: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon, Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser, Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon, BlackRock chief Larry Fink, and Blackstone head Stephen Schwarzman. However, bankers from JPMorgan and Citigroup had already canceled meetings earlier due to safety concerns.

Wall Street executives even consulted security specialists, concerned that high-profile hotels and landmarks could become targets. At the same time, some investors feared that skipping the gathering would offend Saudi officials and business partners.

FII has served as a marquee stage for announcing multi-billion-dollar deals since its debut in 2017. Last year's edition drew more than 9,000 delegates and was linked to agreements, pledges, and projected transactions exceeding 50 billion US dollars.

Blow to Saudi economic ambitions

The postponement deals a significant blow to Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions. FII represents Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's primary showcase to diversify the Kingdom's oil-dependent economy while drawing Western capital into the Middle East.

Saudi Arabia's foreign direct investment stood at only around 33 billion US dollars last year, according to figures cited by Reuters—falling far short of the 100-billion-dollar annual target envisioned by 2030 under the Vision 2030 framework.

The fallout from the Houthi attacks extends beyond FII. The Intersec Saudi Arabia trade fair and the Saudi Retail Forum have also been postponed, the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament has been pushed back to late December, and the fate of the WWE Crown Jewel wrestling event (November 7) has been cast into doubt. FII previously withstood a major boycott in 2018 following the murder of columnist Jamal Khashoggi, with Western business leaders returning a year later. This time, however, the threat giving them pause is missiles.

item.title: Danantara Merges 4 Asset Managers with IDR 143 Trillion in AUM
item.description: Danantara Indonesia has merged four state-owned asset managers holding IDR 143T in AUM, aiming to revamp operations and target global markets.
item.content:encoded:
Merger Completed, AUM Surpasses IDR 143 Trillion

Danantara Indonesia has finalized the merger of four investment management firms within the state-owned enterprises (BUMN, or Badan Usaha Milik Negara) ecosystem. The consolidation was formalized with the signing of the Merger Deed in Jakarta on September 28, 2026.

The four consolidated companies are PT Mandiri Manajemen Investasi, PT BNI Asset Management, PT BRI Manajemen Investasi, and PT PNM Investment Management. PT Mandiri Manajemen Investasi was appointed as the surviving entity, absorbing all assets, liabilities, rights, and obligations of the other three companies.

Collectively, the four firms recorded assets under management (AUM) exceeding IDR 143 trillion as of September 2026. This expanded operational scale is expected to bolster the domestic investment management industry while enhancing competitiveness across regional and international markets.

HR and Technology Transformation Become Top Priorities

Danantara Indonesia Chief Operating Officer Dony Oskaria emphasized that integrating the four companies must be accompanied by the development of an organizational system that is professional, transparent, and equitable. According to him, scaling up operations requires a cultural shift in the workplace, stronger competencies, and enhanced performance.

"Conduct job evaluations, establish job sizing, build a grading system, develop a competency matrix, and define job requirements so that everyone is treated fairly," Dony stated. The restructuring encompasses position appraisals, responsibility classifications, and competency mapping tailored to corporate needs.

Beyond organizational restructuring, harmonizing corporate culture remains a key focus. Dony stressed that a successful consolidation demands alignment in vision, principles, and objectives across all levels of the enterprise. The merger also entails advancing technology infrastructure and elevating investment management standards.

Targeting Retail Investors and the Global Market

In the retail investor segment, the merged entity intends to introduce thematic investment products designed to match public preferences and needs. Distribution will be strengthened by leveraging the network of state-owned banks grouped under the Association of State-Owned Banks (Himbara, or Himpunan Bank Milik Negara).

This initiative aligns with the expansion of the domestic capital market's investor base. As of Friday, August 7, 2026, the number of Single Investor Identification (SID) registrations exceeded 30 million. The steadily growing retail base provides significant runway for the asset management industry to broaden product adoption.

Over the long term, Danantara aims for the consolidated entity to rival global-scale investment institutions. "We aspire to become a global player. If foreign institutions can excel, why can't we? Especially when we possess such an extensive distribution reach," Dony concluded.

item.title: 51 Orangutans Evacuated from W. Kalimantan Fires, 90% Habitat Lost
item.description: A joint team rescued 51 orangutans from wildfire zones in Ketapang and North Kayong, West Kalimantan. Over 90% of PT KALE's conservation habitat was burned; one died from smoke exposure.
item.content:encoded:
51 Orangutans Evacuated from Fire Zones

A total of 51 orangutans have been evacuated by a joint team from the West Kalimantan Natural Resources Conservation Agency (BKSDA - Balai Konservasi Sumber Daya Alam) and International Animal Rescue Indonesia Foundation (YIARI - Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia) from forest and land fire areas in Ketapang and North Kayong Regencies. The rescue operation was conducted from August 6 to October 10, 2026.

More than half, specifically 30 individuals, were found in and around the oil palm plantation of PT KALE. Based on satellite imagery analysis from August 1 to September 25, 2026, over 90 percent of PT KALE's High Conservation Value (HCV) area has burned, destroying the habitat of Bornean orangutans (Pongo pygmaeus) that was previously estimated to be home to around 150 individuals.

Condition of Lusi, Riri, Mama Rian, and Rian

In the latest operations on October 10 and 16, 2026, the team evacuated four orangutans in Ketapang Regency: two juvenile females named Lusi and Riri, as well as a mother and infant named Mama Rian and Rian. Lusi and Riri were found without their mothers in PT KALE's HCV area in Laman Satong Village, while Mama Rian and Rian were rescued from a resident's garden in Riam Berasap Village.

CEO of YIARI and wildlife veterinarian Karmele Llano Sanchez stated that Lusi was found severely stressed, emaciated, dehydrated, and covered in scratches as well as open wounds suspected to be animal bites. 'Lusi looked very stressed and extremely thin. She probably went days without any food in this destroyed forest,' she said.

Meanwhile, Riri was discovered terrified in an oil palm tree with no sign of her mother. This condition is alarming, as orangutan infants generally stay with their mothers until they are around 6–7 years old.

One Orangutan Dead, Conflict Risks Rise

One orangutan named Sempurna was reported dead on August 30, 2026, after being found unconscious in Kuala Satong Village, Ketapang. Pathological examination revealed lung damage suspected to be linked to wildfire smoke exposure.

The loss of forest canopy has left orangutans without shelter and food sources, forcing some animals into plantations or residential settlements in order to survive. This displacement heightens the risk of human-wildlife conflict.

Eight orangutans deemed healthy began being translocated on October 9, 2026, to the Batu Nyambu Protection Forest in Ketapang Regency. The BKSDA and YIARI teams continue rescue operations as several affected orangutans still require evacuation and urgent medical treatment.
